newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases on unmatched dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases on unmatched dlr demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened marginally against the dollar on Thursday as demand for the dollar outstripped supply in the market, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.92 against the dollar from 54.87 on Wednesday, while against the pound, it was posted at 89.69 unchanged.
Dealers said the main support for the dollar drive was from the central bank which was in the market on Wednesday afternoon.
"Whatever dollar inflows came into the market were taken up by the central authorities -- who came in to fund their books," one dealer said.
Some dealers said that the weakening shilling was for the short term mostly because there was support for the shilling at the 54.90 level.
The money market was liquid with low volumes traded. Overnight rates were quoted at 10 percent levels unchanged.
